title: Valparai – Athirappilly Forest Loop
tagline: Coimbatore → Pollachi → Valparai (40 hairpins) → Malakkappara forest road → Athirappilly Falls → Thrissur → Palakkad → Coimbatore. ~400 km in a day, billed as South India's most dangerous road.
summary: A one-day loop that climbs the famous 40-hairpin Valparai ghat, then takes the narrow Valparai–Malakkappara–Athirappilly road across the Anamalai and Sholayar forests — 85–90 km of single-lane tarmac with no fuel, no phone signal and a very real chance of elephants. It drops to Athirappilly Falls, Kerala's biggest waterfall, and returns to Coimbatore across the plains via Thrissur and the Palakkad gap.

credit.note: 'South India's most dangerous road — 400 km in a 1-day trip'

segments.note: Flat, fast, coconut country. Have breakfast in Pollachi; it's the last big town before the hills.
The 40 numbered hairpins start after Aliyar dam. Loop view point at hairpin 9. Lion-tailed macaques near the top.
Tea estates give way to forest. Tamil Nadu forest check post; Kerala check post at Malakkappara.
The 'dangerous' bit: single lane, blind bends, sheer drops, monsoon damage, elephants. No fuel, no signal, no food until Vazhachal.
Back on wide roads. Athirappilly Falls viewpoint is a short walk from the parking.
Four-lane highway through the Palakkad gap. Fast.
Kerala–Tamil Nadu border at Walayar; traffic thickens into Coimbatore.

highlights: The 40 hairpins from Aliyar dam to Valparai — each one numbered, with the Loop view point looking back over the dam.
Valparai tea estates and the Sholayar reservoir, one of the deepest dams in Asia.
The Malakkappara–Athirappilly forest road: 60-odd km of canopy, hornbills, gaur and the occasional elephant.
Athirappilly Falls — 80 ft wide, thundering in the months right after the monsoon.
Vadakkunnathan Temple in Thrissur and Palakkad Fort if you have daylight to spare.

offroad.summary: Tarmac all the way, but the forest stretch is single-lane, badly patched in places and completely unsupported. This is where an ADV with decent ground clearance and knobbly-ish tyres earns its keep.
notes: Valparai ghat hairpins are tight but well-surfaced; the danger is estate buses and Tempo Travellers taking the whole road.
Malakkappara–Athirappilly: potholes and landslide scars, moss on the shaded sections, and gravel at the culverts. Standing on the pegs helps.
Zero fuel between Valparai and Chalakudy (~120 km). Fill to the brim in Valparai.
Zero mobile signal in the forest; download offline maps for the whole loop.
Ride in a group of at least two bikes on the forest stretch — a breakdown there is a long wait.

timings: Forest check posts on the Valparai–Athirappilly road allow two-wheelers roughly 6:00 AM – 4:00 PM only (four-wheelers until 6:00 PM). Be at the Valparai side check post well before 3 PM.
No advance permit; small entry fee (₹20–30 for two-wheelers) and ID check at the check posts.
The forest road is closed intermittently after landslides in the monsoon (Jun–Sep) — check current status before leaving Pollachi.
Fuel: Pollachi, Valparai (last before the forest), then Chalakudy / Athirappilly town. Palakkad and Coimbatore are plentiful.
cautions: Elephants and gaur on the forest road — this stretch has regular human–wildlife incidents. Stop, engine off, reverse if needed. Never get between a calf and the herd.
Do not attempt the forest crossing in rain or fog; the drops are unguarded.
Leave Coimbatore by 5 AM to make the check-post cut-off with time for the falls.
The 'most dangerous road' tag is about isolation and wildlife more than the surface — respect it.
